messages.summary:
## Objective
- Crear un juego RPG 2D completo y jugable en español, con exploración, razas/clases, diálogos, inventario, combate, guardado, crafting, clima, facciones, compañeros, construcción y legado.

## Requirements
- El usuario pidió inicialmente: «Pregunta lo necesario para avanzar».
- La petición de build posterior indica no hacer preguntas, asumir lo razonable y construir el juego ahora.

## Decisions
- Juego web autocontenido, con canvas 2D, interfaz en español y estética de fantasía acogedora.
- Implementación sin dependencias externas obligatorias; guardado mediante `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Creada la interfaz del juego, el mapa y sistemas principales en `index.html`, `style.css` y `game.js`.
- Implementados controles de movimiento, recolección, combate, diálogos, recetas, misiones, reputación, compañero, construcción y legado.
- Añadidos guardado/carga local y soporte de controles táctiles.

### Active
- Corregir errores de sintaxis y verificar el juego en navegador.

### Blocked
- `game.js` no pasa `node --check`: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` en la línea 82.
- La causa aparente es que la línea 47 quedó corrupta: `function setTab(tab){$$('.tab').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>setTab(b.dataset.tab));` reemplazó el cuerpo original de `setTab` y dejó la función sin cerrar; después se introdujo el manejador de pestañas donde debía ir su implementación.

## Next Move
1. Reparar `setTab(tab)` para actualizar clases de pestañas y paneles, cerrando correctamente la función.
2. Ejecutar `node --check game.js` y corregir cualquier error adicional.
3. Probar el juego en navegador, comprobar controles y sistemas, y corregir defectos de ejecución o presentación.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: lógica completa; contiene el error de sintaxis pendiente.
- `index.html`: estructura de la interfaz y canvas.
- `style.css`: estilos y diseño responsive.

## Important Context
- Los cambios están sin commit.
- El último intento de validación fue `node --check game.js`, que falló por el paréntesis inesperado al final del archivo.

## Objective
- Crear un RPG 2D completo y jugable en español, con exploración, combate, progresión y sistemas de mundo persistentes.

- Incluir mundo y exploración, razas, clases, diálogos, inventario, combate, guardado/carga, crafting y recolección, ciclo día/noche y clima, facciones y misiones, compañeros, construcción y legado roguelike opcional.
- Construirlo ahora sin hacer preguntas; asumir lo razonable.

## Decisions
- Juego web autocontenido con canvas 2D e interfaz en español.
- Guardado local con `localStorage`; sin dependencias externas obligatorias.

## Work State
### Completed
- Creados `index.html`, `style.css` y `game.js` con interfaz, mapa y sistemas principales del juego.
- Añadidos controles de teclado y táctiles, misiones, NPCs, recetas, combate, reputación, compañero, construcción y legado.

### Active
- Reparar la sintaxis de `game.js` y validar que la aplicación funciona en navegador.

### Blocked
- `node --check game.js` falla con `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` en la línea 82.
- `setTab(tab)` quedó corrupta en la línea 47: su cuerpo empieza con el manejador de pestañas y no está cerrada correctamente; investigar y corregir el balance de llaves antes de validar de nuevo.

## Next Move
1. Reparar `setTab(tab)` y cualquier error de sintaxis en `game.js`.
2. Ejecutar `node --check game.js` hasta que pase.
3. Probar controles, interacciones y sistemas en navegador; corregir errores de ejecución y presentación.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: lógica completa del juego; contiene el error de sintaxis pendiente.
- `index.html`: interfaz, canvas y paneles del juego.
- `style.css`: estilos y diseño responsive.

## Important Context
- Los cambios están sin commit; `git status --short` mostró archivos nuevos sin seguimiento, incluidos los tres archivos principales del juego.

## Objective
- Crear y dejar funcionando un RPG 2D web autocontenido, jugable en español, con exploración, combate, progresión y sistemas persistentes del mundo.

## Requirements
- Incluir razas, clases, diálogos, inventario, combate, guardado/carga, crafting, recolección, ciclo día/noche, clima, facciones, misiones, compañeros, construcción y legado roguelike opcional.
- Construirlo sin preguntas, asumiendo lo razonable; sin dependencias externas obligatorias.

## Decisions
- Juego web autocontenido con canvas 2D e interfaz en español.
- Guardado local con `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implementados `index.html`, `style.css` y `game.js` con interfaz, mapa y sistemas principales.
- Reparada `setTab(tab)` para alternar paneles; `node --check game.js` pasa.
- Abierta la aplicación en navegador: interfaz, canvas y datos iniciales cargan; sin errores de ejecución observados.

### Active
- Completar pruebas de interacciones y sistemas del juego, además de presentación en escritorio y móvil.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Probar interacciones, controles, combate, crafting y guardado/carga en navegador.
2. Revisar la presentación responsive y corregir problemas detectados.
3. Volver a comprobar `node --check game.js` tras cualquier cambio.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: lógica del juego y reparación de `setTab(tab)`.
- `index.html`: interfaz, canvas y paneles.
- `style.css`: estilos y diseño responsive.

## Important Context
- Los cambios siguen sin commit; los archivos principales aparecen sin seguimiento en `git status`.
- El navegador cargó correctamente; el único error de consola observado fue un 404 de `/favicon.ico`.

## Objective
- Crear y dejar funcionando un RPG 2D web autocontenido, jugable en español, con exploración, combate, progresión y sistemas persistentes del mundo.

## Requirements
- Incluir razas, clases, diálogos, inventario, combate, guardado/carga, crafting, recolección, ciclo día/noche, clima, facciones, misiones, compañeros, construcción y legado roguelike opcional.
- Sin preguntas; asumir lo razonable y evitar dependencias externas obligatorias.

## Decisions
- Juego web autocontenido con canvas 2D e interfaz en español.
- Guardado local con `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implementados `index.html`, `style.css` y `game.js` con interfaz y sistemas principales.
- Reparada `setTab(tab)` para alternar los paneles; `node --check game.js` pasó.
- Aplicación abierta en Chromium; interfaz, canvas y datos iniciales cargaron sin errores de ejecución observados.

### Active
- Probar interacciones, controles, combate, crafting y guardado/carga en navegador.
- Revisar presentación responsive y corregir problemas detectados.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Completar pruebas interactivas en navegador; corregir el comando fallido de `playwright-cli run-code` antes de continuar.
2. Probar controles, combate, crafting, diálogo y guardado/carga, y revisar escritorio y móvil.
3. Volver a ejecutar `node --check game.js` tras cualquier cambio.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: lógica y estado del juego; incluye la reparación de `setTab(tab)`.
- `index.html`: interfaz, canvas y paneles.
- `style.css`: estilos y diseño responsive.

## Important Context
- Cambios sin commit; los archivos principales aparecen sin seguimiento en `git status`.
- Servidor local iniciado en `http://localhost:3002`; navegador abierto en esa página.
- El único error de consola observado fue `404` de `/favicon.ico`.

## Decisions
- Juego web autocontenido con canvas 2D e interfaz en español.

- Implementados `index.html`, `style.css` y `game.js` con interfaz y sistemas principales.

- `game.js`: lógica, estado, entidades del mundo, guardado/carga e interacciones.
- `index.html`: interfaz, canvas y paneles.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element

  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page

  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)

  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog

Navigation:

# Skill: gauntlet-loop

# Gauntlet Loop

The user gives a goal. You give back ONE short prompt they can paste into a fresh agent session.

You are not doing the work. You are writing the prompt that makes another agent grind on the work until it beats a real reference.

## Flow

1. **Read the goal.** One line restatement in your head, not on screen.
2. **Set the bar.** If the user supplied a reference, use it. If not, offer **2 or 3 candidate bars**, one line each, and stop. Wait for their pick. Do not write the prompt yet.
3. **Write the prompt.** One block, paste-ready, no preamble, no headings inside it, no narration after it.
4. **Offer to run it.** One flat line under the prompt: "I can run this here." Not a question.

If they say run it, you become the lead agent and follow the prompt you just wrote.

## The bar is the whole trick

Everything else in a gauntlet loop is scaffolding. The loop only produces quality if the thing it compares against is real.

A bar has to pass three tests:

- **Named.** A specific thing, not a category. "Stripe's pricing page" works. "Award-winning SaaS sites" does not.
- **Fetchable.** The critic can actually get it - screenshot the live page, read the published piece, run the binary, open the repo, watch the footage. If the agent cannot obtain it, it will hallucinate the comparison.
- **Comparable.** Both can sit side by side and a judge can pick one. If you cannot imagine the A/B, it is not a bar.

Bars by goal type:

| Goal | Bar that works |
|---|---|
| Website, app, UI | The live site of a specific best-in-class product, screenshotted at the same viewport |
| Game, 3D, visual | Real footage or screenshots from a named shipped title |
| Writing | A specific published piece by a named author or publication, same length and format |
| Code, tooling | A named repo's implementation, plus its benchmark or test suite as the measurable half |
| Research, analysis | A named analyst report or a paper's methods section, judged on rigour and coverage |
| Deck, doc, deliverable | A real artifact from a firm known for it, same page count |

When you propose bars, prefer the hardest one the agent can genuinely reach. A bar that is too easy makes the loop exit on round one.

If the goal has a measurable half (load time, token cost, benchmark score, word count, pass rate), name it alongside the reference. Taste plus a number beats taste alone.

## Prompt template

Adapt the wording every time. Fill the brackets, keep it short, keep the last line.

```
Build [GOAL].

The bar is [BAR]. Get the real thing first and compare against it directly, not against a description of it.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic inspects the actual output, puts it next to the bar blind with the labels stripped, says which one is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

Rules for what you fill in:

- Bake the bar in as a concrete, fetchable thing. URL, product name, repo, title.
- Add a budget or cost ceiling line **only if the user named one**. No default cap.
- Add tool names only if the goal needs them (image or video generation, a browser, a deploy target).
- Everything else stays out. No architecture, no file layout, no decomposition, no round count, no stack choice unless the user demanded it. The agent decides those, and it decides better than a spec written before the work started.

## Length and voice

Short. Around 120 to 180 words. If the prompt needs a heading to stay readable, it is too long.

Plain sentences. No bullet lists inside the prompt. It should read like someone telling an agent what perfect looks like and refusing to accept less.

## Portability

`/loop` and `ultracode` are Claude Code features. `/loop` reruns the prompt on an interval or lets the model pace itself. `ultracode` opts the turn into multi-agent orchestration.

For any other agent, swap the last two lines for: "Keep looping until the critic picks ours. Run the builders and critics as parallel subagents." The structure carries over unchanged.

## Two filled examples

**Visual goal.** User: "landing page for my running brand, athletic, green and dark, has to feel alive."

Bars offered: A) Nike's current running campaign page B) On Running's homepage C) Gymshark's product landing page. User picks A.

```
Build a landing page for a running brand. Athletic, peak performance, green and dark, energetic, aimed at a young healthy audience. It needs to be interactive and visually unmistakable.

The bar is Nike's current running campaign page. Screenshot it at desktop and mobile and compare against those directly, not against a description of them.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own - hero, motion, type, colour, imagery, interaction, mobile. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic opens the real page in a browser, puts our screenshot next to Nike's blind with the labels stripped, says which is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

**Non-visual goal.** User: "a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for non-engineers."

Bars offered: A) a specific Stripe engineering blog explainer B) a named Julia Evans post C) the Wikipedia article plus a comprehension test. User picks B.

```
Write a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for readers who are smart but not engineers.

The bar is Julia Evans' writing on hard technical topics. Pull three of her actual posts and compare against them directly, not against a description of her style.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be judged on their own - the opening, each explanation, the diagrams, the analogies, the ending. For each piece, fan out a writer and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic reads ours and hers blind with the bylines stripped, says which one a non-engineer would understand faster, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the writer.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

## What breaks a gauntlet loop

- **A vague bar.** The critic invents a comparison and approves everything. Most common failure by far.
- **The builder judging its own work.** The critic must be a separate agent with fresh context. It should not know how hard the builder tried.
- **A soft critic.** Say "harsh" in the prompt and give it a binary job: which one is better, A or B. Scores out of 10 drift upward every round.
- **Named exit after N rounds.** The exit is winning the comparison, or the user stopping the run. Never a round count.
- **Over-specifying.** Every extra instruction is one fewer decision the agent makes with its own judgment. Minimal wins.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element

## Objective
- Rebuild and substantially improve the Spanish-language web RPG while preserving working systems and validating gameplay and responsive layouts.

## Requirements
- Improve overall visual presentation and gameplay holistically.
- Preserve existing functionality and check for regressions.
- Validate desktop and mobile layouts and core gameplay interactions.

## Decisions
- Improve the existing game rather than replacing its systems wholesale.
- Centralize every XP award through `gainXp(amount)`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Centralized XP gains through `gainXp(amount)` for gathering, quest rewards, combat, and trade.
- Fixed gathering and combat level-up feedback.
- Removed manual XP additions and level-up checks outside `gainXp`.
- Fixed the combat `else` syntax error.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.
- Confirmed the live server at `http://127.0.0.1:3000` serves the updated HTML and `game.js`.
- Installed Chromium for browser validation.
- Opened and inspected the game at desktop viewport through Playwright; desktop snapshot and screenshot completed.
- Confirmed the main UI, canvas, inventory, quests, reputation, tools, and responsive mobile controls are rendered.

### Active
- Continue holistic visual and gameplay improvements.
- Exercise core gameplay: movement, gathering, quests, combat, crafting, save/load, and mobile interactions.
- Validate and fix desktop/mobile layout issues.

### Blocked
- Mobile browser layout validation remains pending.
- Full save/load and gameplay interaction testing remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Validate interactions in-browser: movement, gathering, quest creation/completion, combat, crafting, and save/load.
2. Test desktop and mobile viewport layouts, navigation, modals, and touch controls.
3. Fix gameplay or visual regressions discovered during validation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, XP helper, entities, combat, crafting, dialogs, saves, and responsive controls.
- `index.html`: Main interface structure and canvas.
- `style.css`: Desktop, mobile, panel, modal, and canvas styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The live server is active on port `3000`; `start.sh` fails with `EADDRINUSE: address already in use 0.0.0.0:3000` because that port is already occupied.
- Only browser console error observed: `404` for `http://127.0.0.1:3000/favicon.ico`.
- The desktop screenshot was saved under the Playwright output directory.

## Objective
- Continue improving and finish the Spanish-language 2D RPG, preserving existing systems and validating gameplay and responsive layouts.

## Requirements
- Improve visual presentation and gameplay holistically.
- Preserve existing functionality and check for regressions.
- Validate desktop and mobile layouts and core gameplay interactions.
- Keep the experience Spanish-language.

## Decisions
- Improve the existing game rather than replacing its systems wholesale.
- Centralize XP awards through `gainXp(amount)`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Centralized XP gains for gathering, quest rewards, combat, and trade.
- Fixed level-up feedback and a combat syntax error.
- Improved mobile spacing and canvas sizing.
- Embedded a favicon to eliminate `/favicon.ico` 404 responses.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.
- Confirmed the app responds at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`.
- Installed Chromium for Playwright testing.
- Opened the game successfully in the `default` Playwright browser session.
- Confirmed the title, quest creation, crafting recipes, save creation, help modal, and lack of console errors.
- Confirmed mobile layout at 390 × 844 has no horizontal overflow and the canvas ends above the fixed footer.
- Confirmed save data uses `{state:S,entities}` format.

### Active
- Finish save/load, dialogue, combat, crafting, touch-control, desktop, and mobile regression validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete save/load verification using the confirmed `{state:S,entities}` format.
2. Test quest interactions, gathering, crafting, combat, dialogues, trade, character setup, legacy, and construction.
3. Validate desktop and mobile layouts, browser console, and touch controls.
4. Run final syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, XP, quests, combat, crafting, save/load, controls, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Main interface, navigation, canvas, dialogues, favicon, and mobile controls.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile responsive presentation and fixed footer behavior.

## Important Context
- Recent Playwright validation was affected by browser installation state and session restarts, but Chromium was reinstalled and the `default` session was opened successfully.
- The game remains uncommitted unless newer history explicitly indicates otherwise.
- `Saves` are stored in `localStorage` under `verdant-save` as JSON with `state` and `entities`.
- No concrete gameplay regressions or console errors were found in the completed checks.
- Desktop and mobile interaction validation is still pending full completion.

## Objective
- Continue improving and finish the Spanish-language 2D RPG, validating gameplay and responsive layouts from start to finish.

## Requirements
- Improve visuals and gameplay holistically while preserving existing systems.
- Validate desktop and mobile layouts and core gameplay interactions.
- Keep the complete experience in Spanish.
- Perform final syntax and diff checks.

## Decisions
- Improve the existing game rather than replacing its systems wholesale.
- Centralize XP awards through `gainXp(amount)`.
- Keep save data in the `{state:S,entities}` format.

## Work State
### Completed
- Centralized XP gains for gathering, quests, combat, and trade.
- Fixed level-up feedback and the combat syntax error.
- Improved mobile spacing and canvas sizing.
- Embedded a favicon, eliminating `/favicon.ico` 404 responses.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.
- Confirmed the app responds at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`.
- Installed Chromium for Playwright testing.
- Confirmed title, quest creation, crafting recipes, save creation, help modal, and lack of console errors.
- Confirmed mobile layout at 390 × 844 has no horizontal overflow and the canvas ends above the fixed footer.
- Confirmed save/load structure uses `{state:S,entities}`.
- Reopened the game successfully in the `default` Playwright browser session.
- Reinstalled Chromium after the browser executable became missing from the cache.

### Active
- Finish save/load verification using `verdant-save`.
- Test quests, gathering, crafting, combat, dialogue, trade, character setup, legacy, construction, and touch controls.
- Validate desktop and mobile layouts and browser console.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Verify save/load, quest interactions, gathering, crafting, combat, dialogue, trade, character setup, legacy, and construction.
2. Exercise touch controls and final desktop/mobile responsive layouts.
3. Run final syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Game state, XP, quests, combat, crafting, save/load, controls, and rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Interface, canvas, dialogs, navigation, favicon, and mobile controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Desktop/mobile presentation and fixed-footer behavior.

## Important Context
- `Saves` are stored in `localStorage` under `verdant-save` as JSON with `{state:S,entities}`.
- The browser session is currently recoverable, but newer Playwright CLI invocations require valid JavaScript syntax accepted by `run-code`.
- The working tree was clean in the latest status check.

- Validate desktop and mobile layouts and core interactions.

- Preserve saves as `{state:S,entities}` in `localStorage` under `verdant-save`.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: State, entities, XP, quests, combat, crafting, saves, dialogue, construction, and controls.
